events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.44 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The trip was a RydeTAXI metered journey, so distance driven feeds the fare directly and RD-2's metered branch governs: the refund is Σ(extra_km of unexempted segments) × per-km rate = distance_fare ÷ distance_km, i.e. $27.23 ÷ 19.3 km = $1.41/km [F4][F6][RD-2].

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the extra kilometres enter the fare directly; the fare record shows 19.3 km billed at $1.41/km, giving an excess-distance amount of $2.90.

claims.assertion: The rider's claim that she never agreed to any change does not displace the exemption, because RD-4 turns on traffic evidence on the replaced optimal-route section rather than on chat consent; the chat contains no routing request or agreement by either party.

The fare was metered with no surge (1.0x) and no waiting fee: base $3.90, distance $27.23 for 19.3 km, time $7.58 for 29.2 min, platform fee $1.47, totalling $40.18 — every component corresponds to a published, meter-based charge and no unpublished add-on was applied.

The billed excess of $2.90 (2.1 km × $1.41/km) is entirely explained by the exempt segment's 1.73 km plus map-matching residue, and since that segment is exempt the amount is not refundable under RD-2.
claims.void_reason: citation check: cites RD-4(a) — not a citable clause

claims.assertion: The driver's 90-day dispute history shows 1 upheld dispute of 2 and 0 upheld route disputes, so the RD-6 'repeated route deviation' precondition (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no account flag is warranted on this record; profile facts are cited only as an additional-action consideration.

weaknesses: The off-route segment is materially large: 1.73 km added, deviating up to 979 m from the optimal route (F3), which the rider will use to argue the detour was not a minor traffic-induced movement.

The trip total was +2.1 km / +12% over the optimal route and +5.6 min over estimate (F1, F2), so the rider will argue that the whole deviation is unexplained rather than just one segment; only F3 identifies a segment, and the remaining ~0.37 km of excess has no traffic justification on record.

RD-4(a) requires the incident to be on the replaced optimal-route section; F12 places the accident 0 m from the optimal route but the index does not state which sub-section was replaced, so the rider may argue the accident location did not correspond to the segment actually skipped.

The only congestion band evidence is a weak one — Seletar Expressway at band 4 (30–39 km/h) (F10) is not band 1 or 2, and under RD-4(b) band evidence alone cannot exempt a segment, so the case rests on F12.
The driver's own written statement (F9) is a bare assertion of an accident and adds nothing beyond F12; taken alone under the system-record-wins rule it would not carry the exemption.
The rider's complaint of non-consent (F7, F8, F9 show no routing discussion) means the driver has no RD-5 fallback if the traffic exemption on F12 is not accepted.

points.response: Agreed on the segment: F3 shows one off-route segment 17:41–17:44 adding 1.73 km and up to 979 m off the optimal route, which under RD-1 is an unexplained deviation of a material size, not matching noise.

RD-4 does not let the driver substitute his own assertion for record evidence: F12 places the accident 0 m from the optimal route while F10 shows the Seletar Expressway — the road the driver says he used (F9) — at band 4 (30–39 km/h), and RD-4(b) says band evidence alone cannot exempt a segment, so the exemption still has to be shown against the specific 1.73 km section in F3 and on this record it is not.

The fare components are metered and correctly disclosed, we accept that, but RD-2 for a metered trip makes the extra kilometres themselves chargeable only if the segment is exempt — the 1.73 km in F3 produces the $2.90 billed at $1.41/km in F4, and that is exactly the part RD-2 says is not the driver's to keep if RD-1 is breached.

We do not seek a flag_account on this record: F15 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so the RD-6 precondition route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 is not met and the rider's request is confined to the RD-2 refund.

Conceded as to the raw figures — the GPS record does show one off-route segment 17:41–17:44 of 1.76 km versus 0.03 km optimal, adding 1.73 km (F3) — but the segment's existence only triggers the RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 review, and it is exempt under RD-4(a).

points.response: The whole-trip gross figure is not disputed (19.3 km vs 17.3 km, +2.1 km, F1), but RD-2 excludes the non-segment residual (≤0.25 km map-matching residue) and only unexempted segments generate a refund, so the +2.1 km total does not by itself establish a refundable amount.

Conceded that this is a metered RydeTAXI trip where distance enters the fare and that $2.90 corresponds to the billed 2.1 km excess at $1.41/km (F4, F6); but RD-2 makes the refund conditional on an unexempted segment, and the only segment here is exempt under RD-4(a).

Fair weather with 0.0 mm rain (F13) is not evidence against a traffic incident exemption: RD-4 accepts an LTA-reported accident with lanes blocked on the optimal route (F12) as reasonable cause regardless of weather.

notices.text: Good news: we reviewed your trip and found the driver took a detour that added about 1.7 km to your metered fare. You'll get a $2.44 refund, issued as a Ryde voucher on your account. The rest of the trip distance is not refunded, because only the unexplained detour portion of the route counts toward a refund on a metered taxi trip, and the driver had no approved reason for going off the direct route (weather was clear, and no accident or road closure applied to the road actually driven). No action is needed from you.

We reviewed this trip and found one off-route segment that added about 1.7 km to the metered fare, which the shortest-and-most-direct-route rule does not allow. The exemption you described — an accident — was on the route you were supposed to take, not the one you drove, and the speed-band data does not exempt a segment on its own. We are refunding the rider $2.44 as a Ryde voucher. This case also counts as a coaching notice on your account: please follow the most direct route unless there is an approved reason. Your account is not being flagged, since your record shows no repeated upheld route disputes.
